# Chapter 3 — Microsoft Entra ID — The Flat Directory

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
Entra ID's object model and protocol surface, its scalar directory-extension
attributes, and the single architectural fact that shapes everything in this
series: the directory is **flat** — it has no Organizational Unit, no
parent-child container, and therefore no structural inheritance.
:::

## Architecture and Native Capabilities

Microsoft Entra ID, formerly Azure Active Directory, is Microsoft's cloud-native identity platform. It serves as the identity and access management foundation for Microsoft 365, Azure, and any third-party application that supports modern authentication protocols, providing authentication through **OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and SAML 2.0** across both browser-based and API-based access patterns.

Its object model spans several entity types:

* **Users** — cloud-native (created directly in the tenant) or synchronized from on-premises Active Directory.
* **Groups** — security groups (access control and policy targeting), Microsoft 365 groups (collaboration with associated SharePoint, Teams, and Exchange resources), and distribution groups (email distribution).
* **Application registrations** — represent applications that use the Entra ID identity platform.
* **Service principals** — the per-tenant instance of an application registration, carrying the actual permission grants and role assignments for a specific tenant.
* **Managed identities** — system-assigned or user-assigned identities that let Azure workloads authenticate to other Azure services without stored credentials.
* **Device objects** — the device records the platform tracks for compliance and Conditional Access.

The role-based access control model assigns directory roles — Global Administrator, User Administrator, Authentication Administrator, Security Reader, and dozens more — to users, groups, and service principals. Assignments can be direct and permanent, or made eligible through Privileged Identity Management requiring just-in-time activation. Supporting capabilities round out the platform:

* The **unified audit log** captures sign-in and directory-change events, retained for 30–90 days depending on license tier.
* The **Microsoft Graph API** provides comprehensive programmatic access to every directory object through a RESTful interface supporting filtering, paging, and delta queries.
* The **My Apps portal** gives users a consolidated view of assigned applications with SAML and OpenID Connect single sign-on.
* The **B2B collaboration model** invites users from external tenants as guests, granting a cross-tenant identity for shared-resource access without full directory membership.

## Directory Extensions and the Attribute Model

Entra ID supports extending the user, group, device, and application schemas through **directory extension attributes**. Registered to an application registration and expressed as additional properties on the objects they extend, they let organizations store custom attributes — employee classification codes, clearance levels, organizational codes, cost-center identifiers — directly on directory objects, where they become queryable through Graph API and usable in dynamic group membership rules.

> **The ceiling of the attribute model:** Extension attributes are not schema-global in the AD sense — they are tied to the application registration that defines them and must be declared before they can be populated. Their total number is bounded, and the model does not support complex types or structured data: values are string, integer, boolean, or binary scalars. This is sufficient for storing simple organizational *metadata*, but it is not designed to express organizational *hierarchy* or structural relationships between objects.

## What Entra ID Does Not Natively Provide

> **The foundational constraint:** Entra ID has no organizational hierarchy. The directory is flat — every user, group, device, and service principal exists at the same level within the tenant, with no container to inherit from.

```text
Active Directory (hierarchical)        Entra ID (flat)
  domain
  └── OU=Washington                    ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
      ├── OU=Finance                   │ user user user user group group │
      │   └── user (inherits policy)   │ device device sp group user ... │
      └── OU=HR                        │  (all at one level — no OUs,    │
          └── user (inherits policy)   │   no parent-child, no inherit)  │
                                       └─────────────────────────────────┘
```

This is not a limitation of the current release awaiting a future fix. It is a foundational architectural choice: Entra ID was designed as a multi-tenant, globally distributed identity service optimized for authentication and application access — not as a directory information tree in the X.500 tradition. Those are different things, and Entra ID is the former.

[DIAGRAM-01: Structural contrast between a hierarchical Active Directory tree and a flat Entra ID tenant. Left side labeled "Active Directory" shows a branching tree — a domain root over OU=Washington, which splits into OU=Finance and OU=HR, each containing user and computer objects, with a downward arrow labeled "policy inherits down the tree". Right side labeled "Microsoft Entra ID" shows a single flat horizontal plane inside one tenant boundary holding an unstructured row of user, group, device, and service-principal icons, with a caption "one level — no containers, no inheritance". Engineering blueprint style, neutral slate background, federal navy (#1F3A5F) for the AD tree, teal (#1A9E8F) for the Entra plane, monospace labels for OU and object names, no human figures, 16:9 landscape.]

The practical consequence is direct and far-reaching:

* **Delegation cannot follow a subtree.** In Active Directory, a helpdesk administrator delegated to the Washington Division OU manages every user and computer in that OU and every child OU beneath it, with no enumeration of those objects. In Entra ID there is no subtree to delegate over: every delegation is either tenant-wide — the role applies to every object of the applicable type in the tenant — or scoped to an Administrative Unit, a flat container with no inheritance property (discussed separately in Chapter 6).
* **Position is not a native attribute.** A user's organizational position is not a native property of the Entra ID user object. There is no directional parent relationship from a user to the division they belong to, and no mechanism by which assigning a user to a division automatically changes any policy that applies to them.
* **Every assignment is explicit.** Conditional Access, Intune configuration profiles, application access, Entra ID Governance access packages — each is constructed through explicit group membership or explicit object selection, not through positional inference.

The tenant boundary is the only boundary Entra ID natively recognizes. Everything inside it is flat, and everything is governed by explicit assignment rather than structural inheritance.
